title: Finite-algebra permanence of geometrically normal formal fibres
statement: For any commutative Noetherian ring $D$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], define $N(D)$ as follows: for every pair of prime ideals $\mathfrak a\subseteq\mathfrak b$ of $D$, and every finite purely inseparable extension $E/\kappa(\mathfrak a)$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], the ring $E\otimes_D\widehat{D_{\mathfrak b}}$ is normal [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Here $\kappa(\mathfrak a)=\operatorname{Frac}(D/\mathfrak a)$, $D_{\mathfrak b}$ is localization at the prime [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $\widehat{D_{\mathfrak b}}=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}D_{\mathfrak b}/(\mathfrak bD_{\mathfrak b})^n$ is its maximal-ideal-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $D\to E$ factors through $D/\mathfrak a$. Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring satisfying $N(R)$, and let $S$ be a commutative $R$-algebra that is finitely generated as an $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then $S$ is Noetherian and satisfies $N(S)$.

source.place: Tag 0BIV, proposition-finite-type-over-P-ring, specialized to finite algebras and the normal-fibre property of Tag 0BIX, lemma-formal-fibres-normal; Tag 037Z, algebra-lemma-geometrically-normal, finite purely inseparable test.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian], $S$ is Noetherian. Fix primes $\mathfrak a\subseteq\mathfrak b$ of $S$ and a finite purely inseparable extension $E/\kappa_S(\mathfrak a)$. Let $\mathfrak q,\mathfrak p$ be their contractions to $R$; then $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Put $C=\widehat{R_{\mathfrak p}}$ and $H=\widehat{S_{\mathfrak b}}$. The injection $R/\mathfrak q\hookrightarrow S/\mathfrak a$ extends to an injection $k=\kappa_R(\mathfrak q)\hookrightarrow\kappa_S(\mathfrak a)\hookrightarrow E$: a fraction $r/t$ maps to the corresponding quotient, since $t\notin\mathfrak q$ has nonzero image. Thus $E$ is a field extension of $k$, without any assertion that $E/k$ is purely inseparable.

source.place: Tag 0BIT, label lemma-P-ring-goes-up-quasi-finite, proof specialized to finite algebras and geometric normality (Tag 0BIX); use Algebra Tags 07N9 and 037Z.

proof.text: Put $F=k\otimes_R C$. For every finite purely inseparable extension $L/k$, tensor associativity gives $L\otimes_k F\cong L\otimes_R C$, explicitly $\ell\otimes(x\otimes c)\mapsto\ell x\otimes c$, with inverse $\ell\otimes c\mapsto\ell\otimes(1\otimes c)$. The latter ring is normal by $N(R)$ for $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Apply [lem-per-geometric-normality-finite-inseparable-test] to the commutative $k$-algebra $F$. It gives normality of $E\otimes_k F\cong E\otimes_R C$.

source.place: Tag 0BIT, label lemma-P-ring-goes-up-quasi-finite, proof specialized to finite algebras and geometric normality (Tag 0BIX); use Algebra Tags 07N9 and 037Z.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-extension] at $\mathfrak p$. Because $S$ is module-finite, it gives a finite product decomposition $C\otimes_R S\cong H\times B$ as $S$-algebras, by separating the factor indexed by $\mathfrak b$ from the other primes over $\mathfrak p$. The $S$-algebra compatibility is part of the cited statement. In particular tensoring over $S$ uses the same structural maps as the formal fibre in $N(S)$.

source.place: Tag 0BIT, label lemma-P-ring-goes-up-quasi-finite, proof specialized to finite algebras and geometric normality (Tag 0BIX); use Algebra Tags 07N9 and 037Z.

proof.text: Tensor this decomposition with the $S$-algebra $E$. The canonical maps give $E\otimes_R C\cong E\otimes_S(C\otimes_R S)\cong(E\otimes_S H)\times(E\otimes_S B)$. The first isomorphism sends $e\otimes(c\otimes s)$ to $es\otimes c$ and has inverse $e\otimes c\mapsto e\otimes(c\otimes1)$. For the second, send $e\otimes(h,b)$ to $(e\otimes h,e\otimes b)$; its inverse adds the maps induced by $h\mapsto(h,0)$ and $b\mapsto(0,b)$. The orthogonal idempotents $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$ show these maps preserve multiplication and are inverse. Thus $E\otimes_S H$ is a direct factor of the normal ring from Step 2.

source.place: Tag 0BIT, label lemma-P-ring-goes-up-quasi-finite, proof specialized to finite algebras and geometric normality (Tag 0BIX); use Algebra Tags 07N9 and 037Z.

proof.text: A direct factor $T$ of a normal ring $T\times U$ is normal directly from [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]: for any prime $\mathfrak r$ of $T$, the prime $\mathfrak r\times U$ of $T\times U$ has localization canonically isomorphic to $T_{\mathfrak r}$, by projecting fractions to their first coordinate. Its inverse sends $t/s$ to $(t,0)/(s,1)$; the idempotent $(1,0)$ becomes $1$ in this localization. Hence $T_{\mathfrak r}$ is an integrally closed domain. Apply this with $T=E\otimes_S H$. As $\mathfrak a,\mathfrak b,E$ were arbitrary, this proves $N(S)$, together with Noetherianity from Step 1. If $S=0$, there are no primes and $N(S)$ is vacuous.
